# work-log protocol

## Containment (hard)
- All under `<repo>/.agent-research/` — hidden, committed. `notebook/` = index + knowledge;
  `results/N###-slug/` = that entry's outputs. Never `.claude/` or `.agents/`.
- Every figure, table, CSV, log excerpt, one-off script or report goes in that `results/`
  folder; only real project code goes elsewhere.
- Outputs >5 MB stay where produced, referenced by absolute path
  (`notebook/META.md` large_output_location).
- Exception: comparison plots → `.agent-research/plots/<metric>_<date>.png`.
- Hidden dir: ALWAYS explicit `.agent-research/` paths in Glob/Grep/scripts.

## When to log
Only work producing a commit, result, decision or non-obvious lesson, or >~10 tool calls.

## Before
`bin/new-item.sh <type> "<title>"` — exp task fix research analysis writing decision review.
Creates `notebook/items/N###-slug.md` + `results/N###-slug/` + an INDEX row (`open`).

## During
All outputs into that results folder. Experiment: a stated hypothesis with an expected result, a named baseline (the current best), a
kill criterion — before launching; an attempt may change several things at once. Screen on 1 seed
(bar = 2 x noise); >= 3-seed replication at the end of each MAJOR accomplishment. ONE `exp` item per hypothesis. A TRAINING run gets its item AT
SUBMIT (job id, config/branch, gpus x time, log path) and must be registered in wandb with
its job id in the sync lineage — compute nodes have no internet, the login cron is the only
path.
Save every measured value (long csv/json `arm,seed,metric,value[,x]`) here; plot each comparison:
`bin/plot-compare --metric M --csv F --item N### --baseline A`, cite the png (`effect.sh` checks both).
Jobs: preempt + `bin/preempt-run.sh`; GPU-h = rough estimate, no measuring jobs.

## After
1. Fill the item; update the INDEX row (status, one-line outcome, commit hash); append to
   `notebook/log.jsonl`. Closing an attempt at a goal: `bin/effect.sh N### improved|flat|worse|n/a
   [--value V] [--scale knob|module|paradigm]` (improved counts only if it beats GOAL.md best by
   more than its noise; an unlabelled closed exp counts as flat).
2. A result killing a prior belief goes to KNOWLEDGE `## Refuted` with what killed it —
   refutations are findings, never dropped.
3. Edit KNOWLEDGE only if understanding changed — single bullets, never a rewrite:
   `K###: <finding|decision|gotcha> [verified|partial|unverified] (N###; path) {cites:n}`
4. Follow-ups → `notebook/TODO.md`.
5. Every number or claim cites its source (path, command, URL). No source, no claim.

## Housekeeping (advisory)
Mind the `QUOTA` line; clean up every few turns. `.sif` envs, packed data; big → `/hnvme`, small temp → home subdir,
deleted at end; drop stale logs/caches/old ckpts. ORCHESTRATION.md 'Housekeeping'.

## Lint and review
`LINT DUE` from `state.sh`/`new-item.sh` → run `work-lint` immediately, without asking.
`REVIEW DUE` (stall guard: 5 flat attempts in a row vs `notebook/GOAL.md`; `new-item.sh` refuses
exp|task|fix|analysis) → run `work-review` at once. New goal-driven project → `bin/goal.sh init` first.
Details: ORCHESTRATION.md 'Stall guard'.

## Commits, branches, PRs
- Commit ONLY a coherent block (submodule/feature/fix) that is DONE and that control AND
  red-team passed — not mid-change. Code + its `.agent-research/` records in ONE commit,
  `N###: <summary>`; hash into the INDEX row.
- NEVER commit or push on default/main. Working branch only; push per finished block.
- PR gate: list EVERY pipeline the change touches, each with its exact command and exit
  status. Unlisted = unverified = PR blocked. Each must RUN TO COMPLETION on GPU (when GPU
  conditioning is enabled) AND on CPU; GPU-only if the branch clearly profits from GPU.
  Imports and pytest are the writer's job and do NOT count here.
- The PR states the changes and that evidence; resolve every conflict.
- Merges into main are the USER's, by hand. Never merge, never auto-merge.

## Agents — reader + writer per job, cross-model review always
Order: reader -> writer -> control ‖ cross-review. Both reviewers also apply retroactively to
existing code. Keep the source READ-ONLY.
- **While a run is going:** explore — new angles, alternative approaches, agents, cheap tests, `notebook/IDEAS.md`; no idling. ORCHESTRATION.md 'While a job runs'.
- **Several problems at a time:** bundle separable problems into one attempt (no one-variable rule); agents are optional help, never a quota; subagents never own jobs > ~10 min. ORCHESTRATION.md 'Several problems at a time'.
- **reader** (Claude) — studies the source, writes an in-depth implementation spec. No code.
- **writer** (Claude OR Codex) — implements from that spec. Default to Codex for large/bulk/
  high-context jobs (ports, multi-file changes, long reads) — it keeps that reading out of
  Claude's context entirely. Keep small, quick edits with Claude: a Codex job round-trip
  costs more turns than writing three lines. Codex writes only into
  `results/N###-slug/codex/`, never the live tree.
- **control** (**Claude Opus**, or a script) — reads BOTH implementations, checks
  equivalence and, for geometric models, equivariance. Independence comes from the METHOD,
  not the model — so same-family is right and a script is better. Unaffected by who wrote it.
- **cross-review (red-team)** — whichever model did NOT write it: Codex red-teams Claude's
  code, Claude red-teams Codex's landed code (`/code-review` or a general-purpose subagent,
  same adversarial brief either direction). Independence comes from PRIORS; same-family
  review regenerates the same blind spots. Mandatory before anything is acted on or marked
  `[verified]` — not scoped to high-stakes jobs only.
- **integrator** (Claude) — checks Codex's code in `results/N###-slug/codex/` against the
  real tree, adapts it to local conventions, lands it. The only agent that lands Codex code.
- **Two-strike loop** is one trigger among several for routing a job to Codex, not the only
  one: after TWO failed Claude attempts, stop retrying. Codex root-causes, then writes AND
  tests a fix in `results/N###-slug/codex/` — never the live tree — and delivers it with the
  plan. The integrator lands it; Claude then cross-reviews what LANDED. Still broken?
  Repeat, handing Codex every prior round so it gives new ideas.
- **Never act on a reviewer's finding until you reproduce it.** Reviewers REPORT; the main
  agent decides. Reproduce the failure, confound or trivial baseline from the cited
  file/line/command. Confirmed -> fix. Not reproducible -> `[unverified]` with why, and NO
  code change. "Nothing breaks" is likewise not proof — one search that found nothing.
- **Never trust a Codex job's `completed` status** — it is recorded even when the sandbox
  ran no command. Launch with `bin/codex-run.sh` (self-gating; OK or CODEX-UNAVAILABLE), or gate a plugin job with `bin/codex-check.sh <job-id>`. On
  `CODEX-UNAVAILABLE`, fall back to Claude for whichever side (write or review) Codex was
  doing, and note "same-family (codex unavailable)" in the item.
- Only the main agent writes to `notebook/`. Subagents return <=2k tokens and write outputs
  ONLY into the item's `results/` folder — give each its path explicitly.
- Keep records out of auto memory. Contracts + the cross-review prompt: ORCHESTRATION.md.

## Ambiguity
Take the most reversible option, log it in `notebook/SETUP_NOTES.md`, continue. Stop only
if data would be deleted or overwritten.
# Agent orchestration — who reads what, when

## Context is the scarce resource
The main agent's context is the only thing surviving a whole task. Anything entering it that
the next decision does not need is waste; subagents keep large reads OUT. Parallel agents are
OPTIONAL help — use them where independent work exists and they run reliably, never as a quota.

## Read order, any non-trivial task
1. `bin/state.sh` — RULES, last 10 INDEX rows, KNOWLEDGE headline, open TODOs. Always,
   <=25 lines.
2. Only if a row/bullet is relevant: grep that item file or results folder. Never the
   whole notebook. One flat level: INDEX/KNOWLEDGE -> one detail file.
3. Project code: only the files the task touches.
Never re-read what an earlier turn established. The notebook is the memory; re-deriving is
the failure it exists to prevent.

## When to delegate
When the ANSWER is small but the READING is large: sweeping files, scanning logs, surveying
a library, checking a claim across a codebase — OR when the work is independent of what you
are doing now. Not what you can do in two tool calls, and never the judgment itself —
a subagent proposes, the main agent decides.

## Several problems at a time
Do not work one problem per attempt. When the diagnosis shows several separable problems, address them
together: bundle the changes in one attempt (baseline = the current best; ablate only what wins) or run
separate items side by side when the cluster allows. There is no one-variable rule. Reliability rules
that stay (observed failures):
- **Subagents do not own long jobs.** A Bash call tops out at 10 minutes, so a subagent that backgrounds a
  GPU job and returns delivers nothing (2026-10-07: a diagnostic agent "stopped once more on its own
  background GPU work"). For a job > ~10 min the subagent returns a ready-to-submit package; the
  coordinator submits and owns the `wait-job.sh` waiter.
- **Blocked on the user (>25 GPU-h yes, a decision) blocks that item, not the session:** ask in chat, keep
  the other work going.
- **Ending a turn** only when every pending job/agent has a harness-tracked waiter (re-arm one lost in a
  session restart) — otherwise the user has to type "go on".

## While a job runs: no idling
Any long-running work (training run, build, download, agent task) is the moment to widen the search, not to wait. Typical order (do what pays, skip the rest):
1. Read the run's early signals against the stated expectation (cheap; do not touch the job).
2. Ideate: 3-5 NEW angles on the goal — different mechanisms, data, representations, decompositions, framings — not tweaks of the
   running job. Wild or contrarian ideas are explicitly welcome. One line each in `notebook/IDEAS.md`
   (`idea · mechanism · cheapest test · status open|testing|promising|dead(why)`).
3. Agents: literature on the open question, a Codex idea-writer, an outsider or assumption-breaker (the `work-review` step-3
   briefs, lighter). Reports into the item's `agents/` folder.
4. Test the best ideas as far as cheap means allow before any real investment: CPU analyses, ceiling/oracle tests, tiny prototypes,
   cached features, offline evaluation of existing checkpoints, small GPU jobs inside the budget rules (>25 GPU-h still needs a yes;
   GPU only if >=2x a CPU run). Do not compete with the running job for its GPUs.
5. Prepare the next package (pre-registration, scripts, evaluation) so nothing waits when the run ends.
6. Record: promising -> `new-item.sh exp "<title>" module|paradigm`; dead -> IDEAS.md with the reason (and KNOWLEDGE `## Refuted` if it kills a belief).
Quality over quantity: an idea that is only a hyper-parameter of the running job does not count. The stall gate still applies to new
exp items. Ending a turn with a run going is fine once this is done (or there is nothing useful left — say so in the last message).

## The five roles (each names WHO runs it)
Order: reader -> writer -> control ‖ cross-review -> (integrator, when Codex supplied code).
Both reviewers also apply retroactively. Keep the source READ-ONLY.
- **reader** — Claude, read-only. Studies the source, writes an in-depth implementation

- **writer** — **Claude OR Codex**. Implements from that spec. Default to Codex for
  large/bulk/high-context jobs — ports, multi-file changes, long reads — because keeping
  that reading entirely out of Claude's context is the real token-efficiency win: Codex
  runs as a separate process and only a <=2k-token handback re-enters Claude's context,
  which is cheaper than even a Claude subagent. Keep small, quick, single-file edits with
- Push the working branch after every commit and before the session ends; a repo without a remote gets one (private GitHub under Jetzu) or a vault git bundle (`/home/vault/v181bb/v181bb10/git_bundles/`) before any further work. Unpushed = unsaved (user ruling 2026-11-07).
  Claude directly — dispatching, gating (`codex-check.sh`) and integrating a Codex job costs
  more turns than writing three lines. Codex writes only into `results/N###-slug/codex/`,
  never the live tree, regardless of which hat it's wearing.
- **control** — **Claude Opus**, or a script where mechanizable. Reads BOTH implementations
  and checks equivalence, plus equivariance for geometric models; or re-derives the key
  number by a DIFFERENT route. Catches the confident-wrong answer. Its independence comes

  spending Codex here buys almost nothing. Unaffected by who wrote the code.
- **cross-review (red-team)** — **whichever model did NOT write it.** Claude writes ->
  Codex red-teams (`/codex:rescue`). Codex writes -> Claude red-teams (`/code-review` or a
  general-purpose subagent, same adversarial brief). Attacks the conclusion: the confound,
  the tautology, the leak, the trivial baseline that would score the same. Its independence
  comes from PRIORS, the one thing another model family supplies — a same-family reviewer
  regenerates the confounds its own family already considered. Mandatory, not scoped to
  high-stakes jobs: anything acted on or marked `[verified]` gets cross-reviewed by the
  other model, every time.
- **integrator** — Claude. Checks Codex's code in `results/N###-slug/codex/` against the
  real tree, adapts it to local interfaces and conventions, lands it. The only agent that
  lands Codex code. Never copy blindly: a fix built outside the tree misses local context.
Pair reader+writer per job. Add control and cross-review to anything acted on or written to
KNOWLEDGE as `[verified]`.

## Contract for every subagent
State explicitly: (a) the ONE question or change, (b) its results path
`.agent-research/results/N###-slug/`, (c) "write outputs only there, return <=2k tokens,
cite every number with a path or command", (d) what NOT to touch, (e) if it waits on a
job: one backgrounded blocking call, never a repeated check.
Parallel subagents must not write the same file. Launch independent ones in one message;
serialize anything with a dependency.

## Evidence discipline
- Every number carries its source. No source, no claim.
- A subagent's claim is `[unverified]` until a control or a file read confirms it.
- **Reviewers report; the main agent decides.** Never start a fix on a red-team, control or
  Codex finding you have not reproduced FIRST-HAND — open the cited file:line, rerun the
  cited command, build the trivial baseline it claims would score the same. Only a
  reproduced finding starts the fix. If it does not reproduce, say so in the item and leave
  the code alone: a confident reviewer is still a model, and a false positive costs more
  than the review saved. Both ways — "NOTHING BREAKS" is not proof either, just one search
  that found nothing.
- Name a baseline (the current best) and a stated expected result BEFORE the run; add a kill criterion.
  An attempt may change several things at once (no one-variable rule); ablate only what wins. A result
  without a baseline is not a result.
- Replication: screen on ONE seed against the GOAL.md bar (2 x noise). Run the >= 3-seed replication at the
  END OF EACH MAJOR ACCOMPLISHMENT (a new headline number, before it is called verified, committed or put
  in a PR) — not per candidate, not for every small step.
- Before believing a signal, name the trivial explanation that would produce it anyway
  (constant predictor, tautology, shared clock, warm start) and rule it out.
- Save every measured value (all arms/seeds/metrics/steps, long csv/json) in `results/N###-slug/`
  (>5 MB: cite the external path). 10-24: 139/350 closed exps had numbers only in prose.
- Plot every comparison (`bin/plot-compare`, one per comparison+metric) -> `plots/<metric>_<date>.png`,
  cited in the item. `effect.sh --value` refuses the label without both (void/n/a exempt).

## Waiting on long work
**The cost is the TURN, not the sleep.** A backgrounded call burns nothing and re-invokes
you when it exits; a foreground one spends the turn doing nothing. So: background it.

A PreToolUse hook (`~/.claude/hooks/no-noop-wait.sh`) blocks, in the foreground only:
a command that does nothing (`true`, `:`, filler `echo`), one *described* as a wait that
waits on nothing, one leading with `sleep` under 300s, and a loop polling `squeue`/`sacct`.
It allows anything backgrounded, a sleep used as a settle or timeout inside real work, and
heredoc bodies (writing a watcher script is authoring, not polling). Measured against 14,428
real commands from this machine's history: 3.5% blocked, all of them genuine waits. Blocked?
Background it — relabelling or swapping in a different no-op is what it exists to catch.

History: banning waits by name only relocated the spam (`Bash(true)`, `echo .`). Cheapest pattern first:
1. **Harness-tracked work** (Agent, background Bash, Workflow) — no check at all.
2. **SLURM** — be notified, don't poll. One backgrounded call prints every transition and
   the end state with elapsed + exit code:
       Bash(run_in_background=true): bin/wait-job.sh <jobid> [<jobid>...]
   Exit 0 = all COMPLETED; 1 = a FAILED/TIMEOUT/CANCELLED/OOM job, named in the output.
   Pass every job to ONE waiter, not one waiter each.
3. **Other external state** (CI, a remote queue) — ONE backgrounded blocking call.
4. **A deadline you must tick against** — `ScheduleWakeup`/`/loop`/`Monitor`: 5 min floor,
   20-30 min idle, 1200s+ when something else is the real wake signal. Double after two
   consecutive `noop` ticks — a noop reported nothing, so a longer gap loses nothing.

Name the waiter or the interval in every subagent brief that waits on a job (<=10 min foreground
only — longer jobs are the coordinator's: see 'Several problems at a time').

## Jobs: preempt by default
Helma `preempt` (GPU) / `preempt_cpu`: 1 node, 2 d max, default time 10 min (set `--time`), PreemptMode=
CANCEL (never requeued), 15 min SIGTERM->SIGKILL grace, exempt the first 2 h. Use them unless the job is
multi-node, cannot restart, or has a hard deadline (say which on submit).
- Preempt-safe = resume from latest ckpt, ckpt <=30 min (atomic tmp+rename), save+exit on SIGTERM, keep
  latest+best. Wrap: `exec bin/preempt-run.sh -- <cmd>` (`templates/preempt.sbatch`): on SIGTERM/SIGUSR1
  (`--signal=B:USR1@900`) it resubmits the saved batch script `afterany`, forwards SIGTERM, waits. Options
  in `#SBATCH` lines, parameters in env vars (the command line is not replayed). Tested 10-24 (1120092).
- Mock tests: `bin/preempt-selftest.sh`. `wait-job.sh` follows the chain (`~/.claude/state/preempt-chain/<job>.next`). Stop with
  `bin/preempt-cancel.sh` (plain scancel = SIGTERM = resubmit). wandb: glob logs by job name.
- >25 GPU-h ask: rough estimate from known step times; never a measuring job. Preempt counts too.

## Housekeeping: files and quotas (advisory, every few turns)
Quotas bite on FILE COUNT: /home/hpc ~443k soft/543k hard, /hnvme ~61k/81k (grace, then writes fail -
git, logs, ckpts for every project).
- `bin/quota.sh` (15-min cache); `--warn` prints in state.sh and, at most every 30 min per session, the prompt hook at >=90% soft.
- Big files -> `/hnvme`. Many small TEMP files -> home subdir, deleted at task end. Permanent many-file
  sets: pack (LMDB/tar/HDF5/squashfs). Envs/tools: apptainer `.sif`, no new conda/pip trees.
- Every few turns: delete own stale SLURM logs (metrics synced), wandb dirs, caches, core dumps, superseded
  ckpts, scratch/test output. Look first; own project only.

## Stall guard: 5 flat attempts -> project review
Why: Kale closed ~18 exp items (~13 real attempts) after its TM 0.544 plateau (N042) on width, depth,
seeds, encoders, contact-map refiners; TRIAD_v2 spent N022-N041 (4 HARM, 3 VOID, 1 PARTIAL, 2 thin
wins) on low-t canaries. Both were broken only when the USER typed "big ideas". The guard automates that, at
the user's own patience: a replay of both INDEX files (`evidence/2026-10-08/replay_labels.tsv`, borderline labels
flip verdicts) puts both repos at 9/10 when the user stepped in (TRIAD_v2 strict reading: 52 h earlier). Limit 10 -> 5
on 2026-10-24 (user). MUNDANE would not have fired (their work was module-scale).
- `notebook/GOAL.md` (`bin/goal.sh init`): ONE numeric end metric, target + who set it, best, `noise` = 1 sd of
  identical reruns (measured; source named), constraints. Counting starts at `--since` (default: latest item).
- ONE `exp` item per hypothesis (later jobs go into it); `new-item.sh exp "<title>" knob|module|paradigm`.
- Close an attempt: `bin/effect.sh N### improved|flat|worse --value V | --void` (n/a only `--why infra|measurement`).
  `improved` counts only if V beats `best` by > 2 x noise (the believable single-run delta); else flat.
  Unlabelled closed exp = flat; void = flat; scale `?` counts as knob. Ordered by item ID.
- `bin/stall.sh` counts flat/worse in a row since the last `improved` or closed review. At `stall_limit`:
  state.sh + the per-prompt hook print REVIEW DUE and `new-item.sh exp|task|fix|analysis` is REFUSED until a
  `review` item is open AND its `attempts.md` exists. >= 8 of the last 10 attempts knob-level (MUNDANE): knob/unscaled
  exp refused until opened as module/paradigm. A user-requested run overrides with `STALL_OVERRIDE="<their words>"` (logged).
- REVIEW DUE -> `work-review` skill, autonomous. Close with `bin/review-close.sh N###` (checks attempts/diagnosis/
  ideas/declined files, >= 4 agent reports, >= 3 scale-tagged portfolio exps incl. a paradigm one). Review #2 also tells the user plainly.
- Checked by `bin/selftest.sh` (62 cases, incl. the evidence gate: injection, N1000, races, boundaries, gating). No GOAL.md = guard off.

## Compaction survival
Whatever must outlive the session goes in the notebook, not the transcript: the decision,
its reason, the number, the path. Assume the transcript is gone.

## Two-strike loop: Codex builds in its own folder, Claude integrates
Failure rescue is one trigger for routing a job to Codex, not the only one (see below) —
but it still follows this shape. After TWO failed Claude attempts, stop retrying — two
failures mean the approach is wrong and a third try searches the same priors. Codex DOES
write code here, but never into the live tree, so a real tested implementation crosses over
instead of prose while the repo keeps exactly one writer.
1. **Codex** (`/codex:rescue`): give it the problem, ALL prior attempts and why each
   failed, the files, and its folder. It root-causes, writes and TESTS a fix in
   `results/N###-slug/codex/`, and delivers the plan — what it changed, why, what it could
   not test.
2. **integrator** (Claude): check it against the real tree, adapt, land it.
3. **Claude cross-reviews what LANDED** (`/code-review` or a general-purpose subagent, the
   same adversarial brief Codex uses on Claude's code), not what Codex proposed —
   integration is where fixes break.
4. Still broken? Next round with every prior round attached so it gives NEW ideas. When two
   rounds repeat themselves, stop: that is a stall — run `work-review` (it tells the user plainly).
Log per round: hypothesis, what was tested, and what was wrong with the APPROACH — the
durable lesson, not the diff.

## Codex scope and cadence
Codex quota is ample (2026-10-04): a regular writer AND reviewer. A job routed to Codex enters
Claude's context only as a <=2k-token handback — default it for bulk ports, multi-file work, long
reads; keep quick single-file edits with Claude (a Codex round-trip costs more turns than three
lines). Cross-review is UNCONDITIONAL: the model that did NOT write it red-teams it before it is
acted on or marked `[verified]`, any compute request over 25 GPU-h, and at the end of each two-strike round.

**A Codex job can report `completed` having run nothing.** Verified 2026-09-25: four
rescues were recorded `completed` while bwrap failed on every command
(`max_net_namespaces = 0`; fixed, but the failure mode remains). Never read the status
field as evidence — gate every result:
    bin/codex-check.sh <job-id>          # OK, or CODEX-UNAVAILABLE + exit 2
On `CODEX-UNAVAILABLE` or out-of-quota: do not retry Codex, do not skip — rerun the
red-team with a Claude subagent and write "red-team was same-family (codex unavailable)"
in the item. Weaker coverage beats a `[verified]` bullet nothing ever attacked.

## Invoking Codex
**Default: `bin/codex-run.sh <out-dir> <brief-file> [--ro] [--timeout-min N]`**, called with Bash
`run_in_background: true` (you are re-invoked on exit; no user slash command, no polling). Write the
whole prompt (hat, ONE task, contract, paths) to a brief FILE first - it goes in on stdin, so no
quoting traps. `out-dir` = `results/N###-slug/codex/` = Codex's cwd and only writable root. It
runs plain `codex exec` (no plugin broker, no Sonnet forwarder in between), gates itself, and ends
with one line: `OK ...` (exit 0) or `CODEX-UNAVAILABLE <why>` (exit 2 -> redo with Claude, never
skip). Handback = `<out-dir>/codex_last_message.md`; full stream = `codex_run.jsonl`. Gate = a
finished turn + non-empty handback + no quota/model/sandbox/sqlite failure signature (one retry,
transient infrastructure errors only). Resume a thread: `codex exec resume --last` in the same cwd.

Why not the plugin by default (found 2026-10-17): the
`codex:codex-rescue` forwarder is told "if the Bash call fails, return NOTHING" - an empty reply is
a failure, not "no findings"; it takes `cwd` from whatever it parses out of the prompt (a garbled
path was reported as "Codex CLI is not installed"); and every `task` leaves a broker + app-server
alive holding the NFS sqlite DBs - the SessionEnd hook only tears down the broker of the SESSION's
cwd, so brokers started for other workspaces are orphaned for days (one lived 10 days). Fallback if
you do use it: `/codex:rescue` via the Agent tool (`subagent_type: "codex:codex-rescue"`); treat an
empty return as CODEX-UNAVAILABLE. `/codex:transfer|status|result|cancel` are user-only; Claude can
query with `bin/codex-jobs.sh list | result <job-id> | status [--all]` and gate with `bin/codex-check.sh <job-id>`.
Wrapper `~/.local/bin/codex` now also sets `CODEX_SQLITE_HOME` to node-local `/scratch/.privtmp/<user>/codex-sqlite`
(NFS sqlite locks were the likely cause of the intermittent "failed to initialize sqlite state runtime" -
[unverified], not reproducible in 16 parallel launches).
Always name the hat: **write** (implement a spec, build+test in its folder — regular
implementation work, not just rescue), **red-team** (attack, change nothing), or **fix
round** (root-cause + build in its folder, after two Claude failures). A write job gets the
same contract as any subagent (the ONE task, its results path, what not to touch) plus the
spec or source files it needs.

**What to give a red-team — either direction.** Never "review this". Hand it the claim, the
evidence and the paths, and ask it to break the claim. This applies whether Codex is
red-teaming Claude's code or Claude (via `/code-review` or a general-purpose subagent) is
red-teaming Codex's landed code — same brief, model swapped:
  "Claim: <finding, with its number>. Evidence: <paths / commands / config>.
   Do not fix anything. Find why this claim is wrong:
   (a) what trivial baseline — constant, shuffle, copy of the input — gives this same number?
   (b) is it tautological: does a flag, override or shared schedule force what is measured?
   (c) where could the answer leak into the input?
   (d) is it measured at a flattering point — one step, seed, length, best checkpoint?
   Cite file and line per objection. Say NOTHING BREAKS if you find nothing."
Those four are this project's actual failure history (forced `r_seq=t`; step-2000
measurements on a climbing curve; a collapsed Procrustes mean scoring well; recall read as
precision) — ask them every time, regardless of which model wrote the code under review.

Codex output lands like any subagent's: into the item's `results/` folder, `[unverified]`
until a file read confirms it. The plugin's own job logs live outside the notebook
(`~/.claude/plugins/data/codex-openai-codex/state/`) — copy what mattered in, with the job
id, or it is not a record. A Codex/Claude disagreement is itself evidence worth logging.

            self.primary = mu[:512], sd[:512], np.vstack((w[:512, :12], w[-1, :12]))
        else:
            self.primary = replay_markers(self.x, data, t)
        self.secondary = mu[512:], sd[512:], np.r_[w[512:-1, -1], w[-1, -1]]
        # Parity control against stored TT6c outputs, with no measured labels.
        with np.load(Path(args['out'])/'test_preds.npz') as ref:
            i = np.linspace(0, len(ref['gidx']) - 1, 16, dtype=int)
            g = ref['gidx'][i]

                raise ValueError('reference teacher row mismatch')
            actual, _ = self.predict(g)

    def predict(self, rows):
        marker, routes = [], []
        mu, sd, w = self.primary
        mu_a, sd_a, w_a = self.secondary
        for start in range(0, len(rows), 4096):
            r = rows[start:start+4096]
            x = self.x[r].astype(np.float32)
            p = ((x-mu)/sd) @ w[:-1] + w[-1]
            af = ((self.aux[r].astype(np.float32)-mu_a)/sd_a) @ w_a[:-1] + w_a[-1]
            marker.append(np.column_stack((p, af)))
            routes.append((x @ self.head[0].T + self.head[1]).argmax(axis=1))
        p = np.concatenate(marker)
        if not np.isfinite(p).all():
            raise ValueError('nonfinite teacher predictions')

class PBC:
    def __init__(self, data, harness):
        path = data/'external/pbc/PBC_dataset_normal_DIB.zip'
        with zipfile.ZipFile(path) as z:
            names = harness.sorted_names(z, ('.jpg',))

        self.features = np.load(data/'emb/pbc_dinobloom_B.npy', mmap_mode='r')
        self.labels = np.load(data/'emb/pbc_labels.npy', mmap_mode='r')
        self.classes = json.loads((data/'emb/pbc_classes.json').read_text())
        if self.features.shape != (len(names), 768) or self.labels.shape != (len(names),):
            raise ValueError('PBC N008 feature/manifest length mismatch')

    def get(self, records):
        rows = np.array([self.row[name] for _, name, _ in records])
        cls = [r[2] for r in records]
        if [self.classes[i] for i in self.labels[rows]] != cls:
            raise ValueError('PBC N008 label order differs from archive order')
        return self.features[rows]


def limit_per_class(records, n, seed):
    if n is None:
        return records
    classes = np.array([r[2] for r in records])
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    rows = np.sort(np.concatenate([sample(np.flatnonzero(classes == c), n, rng) for c in np.unique(classes)]))
    return [records[i] for i in rows]


@torch.inference_mode()
def embed_mll(data, records, batch_size=16):
    import timm
    model = timm.create_model('vit_base_patch14_dinov2', pretrained=False, num_classes=0, img_size=224)
    ck = torch.load(data/'models/DinoBloom-B.pth', map_location='cpu', weights_only=True)['teacher']
    model.load_state_dict({k[9:]: v for k, v in ck.items() if k.startswith('backbone.') and k != 'backbone.mask_token'})
    del ck
    model.eval()
    mean = torch.tensor([.485, .456, .406])[:, None, None]
    sd = torch.tensor([.229, .224, .225])[:, None, None]
    features = []
    with ExitStack() as stack:
        archives = {p: stack.enter_context(zipfile.ZipFile(p)) for p in sorted({p for p, _, _ in records})}
        for start in range(0, len(records), batch_size):
            batch = []
            for path, name, _ in records[start:start+batch_size]:
                with Image.open(io.BytesIO(archives[path].read(name))) as im:
                    x = torch.from_numpy(np.asarray(im.convert('RGB'), dtype=np.float32) / 255).permute(2, 0, 1)
                batch.append(F.interpolate(x[None], size=224, mode='bilinear', antialias=True)[0])
            features.append(model((torch.stack(batch)-mean)/sd).numpy())
    return np.concatenate(features)

#!/usr/bin/env -S python3 -I -B
"""Score two class-conditioned GS students with the registered N058 clinical contrasts."""
import argparse
import csv
import hashlib
import importlib.util
import json
from pathlib import Path
import sys
import tempfile

import numpy as np
import torch
from threadpoolctl import threadpool_limits

HERE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
sys.path.insert(0, str(HERE))
from n093_data import PBC, Teacher, archived_ridge, embed_mll, limit_per_class, partition, targets
from n093_match import CLASSES, Students, sample

DATA = Path('/hnvme/workspace/v181bb10-bsccm')
HARNESS = HERE.parents[1]/'N058-confirm-hub-tt6c-on-mll23-fine-contrasts/code'


def load_harness(directory):
    spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location('n058_eval', directory/'n056_eval.py')
    module = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
    spec.loader.exec_module(module)
    if tuple(module.tr.ANCH) != CLASSES:
        raise ValueError('registered PBC anchors changed')
    return module


def correlation(p, y):
    ok = np.isfinite(p) & np.isfinite(y)
    x, y = p[ok].astype(np.float64), y[ok].astype(np.float64)
    r = None if len(x) < 3 or min(x.std(), y.std()) < 1e-10 else float(np.corrcoef(x, y)[0, 1])
    return r, len(x)


def macro(rows, arm, teacher, seed):
    out = dict(arm=arm, teacher=teacher, seed=seed)
    for key, selected, expected in (
        ('MLL23_15', [r for r in rows if r['domain'] == 'MLL23'], 15),
        ('primary16', [r for r in rows if r['primary']], 16),
        ('PBC10', [r for r in rows if r['domain'] == 'PBC'], 10),
        ('all25', rows, 25),
    ):
        if len(selected) != expected or len({(r['domain'], r['contrast']) for r in selected}) != expected:
            raise ValueError(f'incomplete contrast dictionary: {key}')
        scores = [r['auroc'] for r in selected]
        if any(x is None or not np.isfinite(x) for x in scores):
            raise ValueError(f'missing contrast support: {key}')
        out[key] = float(np.mean(scores))
    return dict(**out, n=len(rows))


def csv_file(path, rows):
    with path.open('w', newline='') as f:
        writer = csv.DictWriter(f, fieldnames=list(rows[0]))
        writer.writeheader()
        writer.writerows(rows)


def digest_ids(ids):
    return hashlib.sha256('\n'.join(map(str, ids)).encode()).hexdigest()


def eval_features(a, harness, pbc, fit_ids):
    clinical, audit = {}, {}
    for domain in ('PBC', 'MLL23'):
        records = harness.clinical_manifest(a.data, domain, 'eval')
        ids = harness.record_ids(records)
        if len(set(ids)) != len(ids) or set(ids).intersection(fit_ids):
            raise ValueError('duplicate evaluation ID or anchor overlap')
        # Compare the complete evaluation universe to the actual registered T run.
        with np.load(a.data/f'runs/n058_main/t0/T_s0/{domain}_T_pred.npz') as ref:
            if not np.array_equal(ids, ref['ids']):
                raise ValueError(f'{domain} manifest differs from N058')
        selected = limit_per_class(records, 2 if a.smoke else None, 93)
        x = pbc.get(selected) if domain == 'PBC' else embed_mll(a.data, selected)
        clinical[domain] = x, np.array([r[2] for r in selected])
        audit[domain] = dict(registered_n=len(ids), scored_n=len(x), registered_sha256=digest_ids(ids),
                             scored_sha256=digest_ids(harness.record_ids(selected)))
    return clinical, audit


def run(a, out):
    harness = load_harness(a.harness)
    t = targets(a.data)
    names = list(t['names'])
    pairs = {p['teacher']: p for p in json.loads((a.harness/'teachers.json').read_text()) if p['seed'] == 0}
    if set(pairs) != {'t0', 't1', 't2'}:
        raise ValueError('incomplete seed-0 teacher registry')
    gs_feats = np.load(a.data/'emb/giemsa_dinobloom_B.npy', mmap_mode='r')
    if gs_feats.shape != (15712, 768):
        raise ValueError('unexpected GS feature schema')
    pbc = PBC(a.data, harness)
    fit = [r for r in harness.clinical_manifest(a.data, 'PBC', 'fit') if r[2] in CLASSES]
    fit = limit_per_class(fit, 16 if a.smoke else None, a.seed)
    fit_ids = harness.record_ids(fit)
    anchors = pbc.get(fit)
    labels = np.array([CLASSES.index(r[2]) for r in fit])

    archive = archived_ridge(a.data)
    bundles, audit = {}, dict(mode='CPU_SMOKE' if a.smoke else 'FULL', seed=a.seed, anchor_n=len(anchors),
                              anchor_ids_sha256=digest_ids(fit_ids), teachers={}, folds={})
    for teacher in a.teachers:
        lf = Teacher(pairs[teacher], a.data, t, archive)
        audit['teachers'][teacher] = lf.audit
        for holdout in a.holdouts:
            gs, bank, test = partition(t, holdout)
            rng = np.random.default_rng(93 + holdout)
            gs = sample(gs, 32 if a.smoke else None, rng)
            bank = sample(bank, 96 if a.smoke else None, rng)
            test = sample(test, 24 if a.smoke else None, rng)
            marker, lf_class = lf.predict(bank)
            student = Students(anchors, labels, a.seed).fit(gs_feats[t['hist_row'][gs]], marker, lf_class)
            # The LF features of evaluation cells enter only this held-out comparison.
            reference, _ = lf.predict(test)
            bundles[teacher, holdout] = student, test, reference
            audit['folds'][f'{teacher}/holdout{holdout}'] = dict(holdout_slide=int(t['slide'][test[0]]),
                training_gs=len(gs), training_lf=len(bank), test_gs=len(test), gs_sha256=digest_ids(gs),
                bank_sha256=digest_ids(bank), test_sha256=digest_ids(test), classes=student.audit)

    clinical, audit['clinical'] = eval_features(a, harness, pbc, fit_ids)
    for holdout in a.holdouts:
        folder = out/f'holdout{holdout}'
        folder.mkdir()
        per_run, contrasts, sanity, agreement = [], [], [], []
        for teacher in a.teachers:
            student, rows, reference = bundles[teacher, holdout]
            scores = {arm: [] for arm in ('F1', 'F2')}
            for domain, (x, y) in clinical.items():
                predictions, _ = student.predict(x)
                for arm, pred in predictions.items():
                    for row in harness.score_contrasts(pred, y, names, domain):
                        scores[arm].append(dict(**row, arm=arm, teacher=teacher, seed=a.seed))
            pred, route = student.predict(gs_feats[t['hist_row'][rows]])
            observed = t['observed'][rows]
            slide = int(t['slide'][rows[0]])
            for arm, values in pred.items():
                per_run.append(macro(scores[arm], arm, teacher, a.seed))
                contrasts.extend(scores[arm])
                fields = dict(arm=arm, teacher=teacher, seed=a.seed, holdout=holdout, slide=slide)
                r, n = correlation(values[observed, -1], t['autofl'][rows[observed]])
                sanity.append(dict(**fields, target='autofl', n=n, autofl_r=r))
                for j, name in enumerate(names[:-1]):
                    r, n = correlation(values[:, j], reference[:, j])
                    agreement.append(dict(**fields, marker=name, n=n, r_student_teacher=r))
            np.savez_compressed(folder/f'{teacher}_paired.npz', global_row=rows, hist_row=t['hist_row'][rows],
                                names=t['names'], F1=pred['F1'], F2=pred['F2'], route=route, teacher=reference,
                                autofl=t['autofl'][rows], autofl_observed=observed)
        prefix = 'smoke_' if a.smoke else 'n093_'
        csv_file(folder/(prefix+'per_run.csv'), per_run)
        csv_file(folder/'contrasts.csv', contrasts)
        csv_file(folder/'sanity.csv', sanity)
        csv_file(folder/'agreement.csv', agreement)
    (out/'audit.json').write_text(json.dumps(audit, indent=2, allow_nan=False)+'\n')
    return audit


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument('--data', type=Path, default=DATA)
    parser.add_argument('--harness', type=Path, default=HARNESS)
    parser.add_argument('--out', type=Path, required=True, help='new output directory')
    parser.add_argument('--teachers', choices=('t0', 't1', 't2'), nargs='+')
    parser.add_argument('--holdouts', choices=(0, 1), type=int, nargs='+')
    parser.add_argument('--seed', type=int, default=0)
    parser.add_argument('--threads', type=int)
    parser.add_argument('--smoke', action='store_true', help='bounded real t0 integration test')
    a = parser.parse_args()
    a.teachers = a.teachers or (['t0'] if a.smoke else ['t0', 't1', 't2'])
    a.holdouts = a.holdouts or ([1] if a.smoke else [1, 0])
    if len(set(a.teachers)) != len(a.teachers) or len(set(a.holdouts)) != len(a.holdouts):
        parser.error('duplicate teachers/holdouts')
    if a.smoke and (a.teachers != ['t0'] or len(a.holdouts) != 1):
        parser.error('smoke uses the archived t0 ridge and one held-out slide')
    threads = a.threads if a.threads is not None else (4 if a.smoke else 48)
    if threads < 1 or a.seed < 0:
        parser.error('threads must be positive and seed nonnegative')
    if a.out.exists():
        parser.error('choose a new output directory')
    a.out.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    torch.set_num_threads(threads)
    with threadpool_limits(limits=threads), tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(dir=a.out.parent) as tmp:
        stage = Path(tmp)/'run'
        stage.mkdir()
        audit = run(a, stage)
        stage.rename(a.out)
    print(f"{audit['mode']} passed: {len(a.teachers)} teachers, holdouts {a.holdouts}, {a.out}")


if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()

# N093 · Class-conditional Giemsa to marker matching

F1 predicts a soft mixture of three LF-teacher class means. F2 assigns a GS image to one of the three classes and predicts a weighted average of LF-teacher profiles from that class. Each profile has the twelve TT6c marker outputs and the shared auxiliary autofluorescence output. Both students take a frozen 768-dimensional DinoBloom-B image embedding as their only inference input.

## Classes and training cells

| PBC half-A anchor | BSCCM LF head output | Contributing BSCCM cls10 gates |
|---|---|---|
| lymphocyte | 0 · lymphocyte | 0 |
| neutrophil | 1 · granulocyte | 1, 2, 3 |
| monocyte | 2 · monocyte | 7, 8, 9 |

Neutrophil is the harness's morphology anchor for the broader granulocyte gate. The remaining five PBC classes have no training role. Clinical cells outside the three anchored classes still receive predictions. This is coarse-lineage matching, with class assignment error possible on both sides. Gates and their grouping come from the repository's `scripts/make_targets_v3.py`. N008 previously observed a large PBC-to-BSCCM shift. The fold audit therefore records the number of BSCCM GS cells assigned to each route.

The GS classifier is multinomial logistic regression (`C=0.1`) on standardized PBC-A anchor embeddings. Both scaler and classifier fit only the registered, duplicate-filtered anchors. The PBC feature row is its position in the original sorted archive listing from `scripts/embed_external.py`. The N058 harness performs the alternating split before removing duplicates. The loader checks labels against archive names for the rows it takes.

Each fold uses split-0 GS cells and split-0 non-GS LF cells from the source draw. The LF bank includes single-marker, pooled and unstained acquisitions. Every entry carries the teacher's whole predicted profile. F1 uses **every** eligible bank entry. Each registered marker encoder supplies its own trained linear `c3` head on raw 512-dimensional LF features. The implementation also handles an absent head by fitting a classifier on draw-0, split-0, pooled, singly gated `cls3` rows from slides outside both GS slides. The registered t0–t2 runs all have the head.

## Within-class OT

GS and marker vectors have different dimensions and unrelated axes. F2 describes each cell by its distances to the three corresponding class centroids in its own modality. On the GS side the centroids use labeled PBC-A anchors in standardized embedding space. On the LF side they use the routed LF bank in standardized teacher-output space.

Within each class the GS support combines source-slide GS cells routed by the classifier and PBC-A cells carrying that anchor label. The LF support contains only bank cells routed to that class by the teacher. With seed 0 by default, F2 samples up to 1,024 rows uniformly without replacement on each side of each class. It converts each of the three distances to its empirical midrank within that support. The cost is mean squared distance between the two rank vectors. POT Sinkhorn fits uniform marginals with entropy regularization 0.035. The solver checks both marginals. For a new GS image, the frozen GS rank functions and fitted LF column potential give the conditional transport weights. Their barycentre uses the original LF marker values. No evaluation-batch statistics enter either student. The assumption that corresponding within-class distance ranks carry similar biology is testable with the held-out metrics.

## Teacher and endpoint provenance

- The seed-0 entries of N058's `code/teachers.json` specify the three marker feature sources and the common v6c auxiliary source. Each run checks the TT6c configuration hash, LF encoder configuration, global row maps and registered target order. The GS student's regression head is never used to generate a marker bank.
- The original TT6c marker teacher is a per-output ridge on v4c LF features. For t0 the program reads the N054 A0 frozen ridge from the seekable archive `runs/archive_n054v3_n057_runs.tar`, member `n054v3_batch1/A0/baseline_teacher.npz`, and verifies its SHA-256. This member also supplies the shared v6c autofluorescence ridge for all three teachers.
- For t1 and t2 the program reconstructs the registered marker ridge with the corresponding LF features, original marker masks, split-0 stained normalization, per-marker seed, 60,000-row cap, unpenalized intercept and ridge penalty 10. It checks that these label rows exclude both GS slides. All teachers undergo a fixed numerical parity check against sixteen original TT6c saved teacher predictions (absolute tolerance 0.02 in the saved output units). CPU and original GPU arithmetic can differ. The smoke audit records t0's maximum difference of 0.00257.
- Induction applies to the new students. The historical LF teachers are frozen references from FOV-split training on both draws. Their training excluded all GS-paired cells, and the shared auxiliary teacher used other non-GS cells on both unstained slides. The provided frozen GS features also retain their original intensity preprocessing. A completely new-draw LF-teacher experiment would require different teachers.
- Both students are fitted before loading clinical evaluation features. Scoring uses N058's own `clinical_manifest`, `score_contrasts` and primary flags. It checks the ordered evaluation IDs against the saved N058 T run (8,538 PBC-B and 7,265 MLL23) and disjointness from anchor IDs. MLL23 evaluation images use the N008 frozen DinoBloom-B single-view preprocessing, computed once on CPU across teachers/folds. Historical T/H used eight-view inference. Endpoint and case membership match.
- N054 M1 is within-slide Pearson correlation against observed same-cell detrended v6c autofluorescence, with all FOV splits on the held-out slide. The other twelve correlations compare GS predictions to the paired cell's own LF-teacher output in global-row order. They measure teacher agreement. Missing or constant Pearson inputs produce a blank coefficient with its finite-pair count.

# N093 · Class-conditional Giemsa to marker matching

F1 predicts a soft mixture of three LF-teacher class means. F2 assigns a GS image to one of the three classes and predicts a weighted average of LF-teacher profiles from that class. Each profile has the twelve TT6c marker outputs and the shared auxiliary autofluorescence output. Both students take a frozen 768-dimensional DinoBloom-B image embedding as their only inference input.

## Classes and training cells

| PBC half-A anchor | BSCCM LF head output | Contributing BSCCM cls10 gates |
|---|---|---|
| lymphocyte | 0 · lymphocyte | 0 |
| neutrophil | 1 · granulocyte | 1, 2, 3 |
| monocyte | 2 · monocyte | 7, 8, 9 |

Neutrophil is the harness's morphology anchor for the broader granulocyte gate. The remaining five PBC classes have no training role. Clinical cells outside the three anchored classes still receive predictions. This is coarse-lineage matching, with class assignment error possible on both sides. Gates and their grouping come from the repository's `scripts/make_targets_v3.py`. N008 previously observed a large PBC-to-BSCCM shift. The fold audit therefore records the number of BSCCM GS cells assigned to each route.

The GS classifier is multinomial logistic regression (`C=0.1`) on standardized PBC-A anchor embeddings. Both scaler and classifier fit only the registered, duplicate-filtered anchors. The PBC feature row is its position in the original sorted archive listing from `scripts/embed_external.py`. The N058 harness performs the alternating split before removing duplicates. The loader checks labels against archive names for the rows it takes.

Each fold uses split-0 GS cells and split-0 non-GS LF cells from the source draw. The LF bank includes single-marker, pooled and unstained acquisitions. Every entry carries the teacher's whole predicted profile. F1 uses **every** eligible bank entry. Each registered marker encoder supplies its own trained linear `c3` head on raw 512-dimensional LF features. The implementation also handles an absent head by fitting a classifier on draw-0, split-0, pooled, singly gated `cls3` rows from slides outside both GS slides. The registered t0–t2 runs all have the head.

## Within-class OT

GS and marker vectors have different dimensions and unrelated axes. F2 describes each cell by its distances to the three corresponding class centroids in its own modality. On the GS side the centroids use labeled PBC-A anchors in standardized embedding space. On the LF side they use the routed LF bank in standardized teacher-output space.

Within each class the GS support combines source-slide GS cells routed by the classifier and PBC-A cells carrying that anchor label. The LF support contains only bank cells routed to that class by the teacher. With seed 0 by default, F2 samples up to 1,024 rows uniformly without replacement on each side of each class. It converts each of the three distances to its empirical midrank within that support. The cost is mean squared distance between the two rank vectors. POT Sinkhorn fits uniform marginals with entropy regularization 0.035. The solver checks both marginals. For a new GS image, the frozen GS rank functions and fitted LF column potential give the conditional transport weights. Their barycentre uses the original LF marker values. No evaluation-batch statistics enter either student. The assumption that corresponding within-class distance ranks carry similar biology is testable with the held-out metrics.

## Teacher and endpoint provenance

- The seed-0 entries of N058's `code/teachers.json` specify the three marker feature sources and the common v6c auxiliary source. Each run checks the TT6c configuration hash, LF encoder configuration, global row maps and registered target order. The GS student's regression head is never used to generate a marker bank.

For t0 the program reads the N054 A0 frozen ridge from the seekable archive `runs/archive_n054v3_n057_runs.tar`, member `n054v3_batch1/A0/baseline_teacher.npz`, and verifies its SHA-256. This member also supplies the shared v6c autofluorescence ridge for all three teachers.
- For t1 and t2 the program reconstructs the registered marker ridge with the corresponding LF features, original marker masks, split-0 stained normalization, per-marker seed, 60,000-row cap, unpenalized intercept and ridge penalty 10. It checks that these label rows exclude both GS slides. CPU and original GPU arithmetic can differ. The smoke audit records t0's maximum difference of 0.00257.

Their training excluded all GS-paired cells, and the shared auxiliary teacher used other non-GS cells on both unstained slides. The provided frozen GS features also retain their original intensity preprocessing. A completely new-draw LF-teacher experiment would require different teachers.
